Fixed choices: keep Streamlit as frontend; add separate FastAPI backend; provide MCP over Streamable HTTP; migrate all current functionality preserving behavior. Make folders/README explain technologies and runtime flow. Design future identity/auth, billing, and additional modules without modifying unrelated modules. Target: apps/web (Streamlit UI and HTTP API client only), apps/api (FastAPI REST/BFF), apps/mcp-server (MCP server / Streamable HTTP tools), packages/contracts (versioned request/response schemas), backend/modules/{reading,writing,tutor,exam_library,identity,billing} with extensible module entrypoints and explicit api/application/domain/infrastructure boundaries where justified; backend/platform for dependency wiring/policies/events; infrastructure adapters for SQLite and external Groq LLM. Baseline 123 passed, 2 unrelated failures: tests/test_article_ingestion.py::test_crawl_imports_eligible_full_text_and_skips_duplicate and tests/test_tutor.py::test_tutor_saves_lemma_and_inflection_from_grammar_answer. title: Streamlit YKI Coach Rearchitecture

assessment_snapshot.intro: The supplied project profile describes a Python/Streamlit YKI Reading AI Coach with:
bullets: Existing folders for AI/LLM integration, SQLite persistence, models, repositories, services, exam ingestion, tests, and Streamlit views.
The requested target separates Streamlit UI, FastAPI REST/BFF, MCP Streamable HTTP, shared contracts, modular backend use cases, and infrastructure adapters.
The profile warns that pre-existing user changes and application data must be preserved; no source inspection was performed for this clarification gate.

proposed_outcome: Rearchitect the application in the current repository with Streamlit retained as an HTTP-client-only frontend, a separate FastAPI REST/BFF and MCP Streamable HTTP server sharing application use cases through versioned contracts, modular domain boundaries and SQLite/Groq adapters, while preserving all current behaviors, legal/consent handling, runnability, and the explicit data, environment, and git constraints. Identity and billing remain disabled extension points, not functioning features.
